name: Filter bar
summary: The row above a table: search, filter chips with one applied and removable, add a filter, a sort button and the number of results; on a phone the search goes full width and the chips wrap onto rows at their natural width.
use: above a table people search, filter and sort
a11y: The bar is a labelled search landmark; every chip and the sort control are buttons that say they open a popup, the remove button names the filter it clears, and the result count is a polite live region.

use_when: above a list of cards or search results that people narrow by a few fields
avoid_when: searching across the whole app or running commands: use command-menu
switching between views of the same page: use page-header-tabs

parts.name: search
parts.what: the search field, with a shortcut hint

parts.name: applied
parts.what: an applied filter: its name and value, plus a remove button

parts.name: remove
parts.what: removes the applied filter it sits in

parts.name: filters
parts.what: one filter not yet applied, which opens its options

parts.name: sort
parts.what: the current sort order, which opens a menu

empty.how: when the count is 0, keep the bar as it is and put empty-state under it with a button that removes every applied filter

loading.how: while results reload, replace the count with a short grey block and keep the chips usable

error.how: if results fail to load, show 'Could not load' in place of the count and an alert-banners line under the bar

disabled.how: while the table loads, set disabled on the filter chips and Sort and dim them

overflow.how: chips wrap onto more rows at their natural width; under 900 px they move to their own row, and on a phone the search goes full width

long_text.how: chip, count and sort labels never wrap; a long chip drops to its own row, so keep each label short

keyboard: Tab moves through the search field, each chip and its remove button, Add filter, then Sort
Enter or Space on a remove button clears that filter, turns it back into a plain chip and moves focus to it; the new count is read out
